description: DASE: an attack-decay envelope whose attack share is modulated by the audio fed into it, so it works as a VCA and a wave shaper, with an internal oscillator adding repeated attacks or tremolo

params.text: Sets the length of the whole envelope, 0.03125 to 32 seconds with 1 second at noon
Sets the share of the envelope given to the attack, the rest being the decay: 0% is a falling ramp, 50% a triangle and 100% a rising ramp
Attenuates the IN jack before it modulates the attack share, which sets the output volume; 0% to 100%, starting at 100%
Bends the attack and decay stages, concave down fully counter-clockwise, linear at noon and concave up fully clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the ENVELOPE LENGTH CV input, where each volt doubles or halves the length
Attenuates and inverts the ENVELOPE ATTACK CV input, scaled at 10% per volt with the attenuverter at 100%
Attenuates and inverts the INPUT LEVEL CV input, scaled at 10% per volt with the attenuverter at 100%
Attenuates and inverts the OUTPUT RESPONSE CV input, scaled at 0.1 per volt with the attenuverter at 100%
Cycles what a trigger does while an envelope is running: yellow starts the attack from the level reached, light blue restarts from 0V, and dark grey ignores triggers until the envelope has finished
Turned on, each polyphonic channel gets its own repeat oscillator that restarts when that channel is triggered; turned off one free-running oscillator drives every channel
Cycles the oversampling applied against aliasing: off, then x2, x4, x8, x16 and x32
Turned on, the output is DC coupled and unipolar; turned off it is AC coupled and bipolar
Sets the rate of the repeat oscillator, 7.5 to 1920 BPM with 120 BPM at noon
Sets the depth of the repeat modulation, -1 to 1 with no modulation at noon; the two directions invert the shape against each other
Sets the share of the repeat oscillator's cycle given to its attack: 0% is a falling ramp, 50% a triangle and 100% a rising ramp
Attenuates and inverts the REPEAT RATE CV input, which is a volt per octave with the attenuverter at 100%
Attenuates and inverts the REPEAT LEVEL CV input, scaled at 0.1 per volt with the attenuverter at 100%
Attenuates and inverts the REPEAT ATTACK CV input, scaled at 10% per volt with the attenuverter at 100%

inputs.text: Lengthens and shortens the envelope, added to the ENVELOPE LENGTH knob through the attenuverter beside it; the total is held between 0.03125 and 32 seconds
Moves the attack share, added to the ENVELOPE ATTACK knob through the attenuverter beside it; the total is held between 0% and 100%
Moves the input attenuation, added to the INPUT LEVEL knob through the attenuverter beside it
Bends the attack and decay curves, added to the OUTPUT RESPONSE knob through the attenuverter beside it; the total is held between -1 and 1
Changes the rate of the repeat oscillator, added to the REPEAT RATE knob through the attenuverter beside it; this jack reads channel one only
Changes the depth of the repeat modulation, added to the REPEAT LEVEL knob through the attenuverter beside it; the total is held between -1 and 1 and this jack reads channel one only
Moves the attack share of the repeat oscillator, added to the REPEAT ATTACK knob through the attenuverter beside it; the total is held between 0% and 100%, and this jack reads channel one only
A rising edge starts the envelope; it reads high above 2V and low below 0.2V
The audio put through the envelope, and the signal whose instantaneous voltage modulates the attack share, which is what shapes the output waveform

outputs.text: The audio after the envelope, bipolar and AC coupled, or unipolar and DC coupled with the DC button on

notes: nothing comes out until a trigger arrives at TRIG; the envelope runs once for each rising edge
the three repeat oscillator CV jacks are monophonic; every other jack takes polyphony, and the output carries as many channels as the widest input
